body:
`.github/policy/tier-policy.config` opens "Auto-merge tier policy — single source
of truth" and lists three consumers. For TIER1_PATHS_REGEX that is not true.

Every reference to it, repo-wide:

    .github/policy/tier-policy.config:31   the declaration
    scripts/lib/tier_policy.py:45          a frozen historical fallback
    scripts/lib/tier_policy.py:76,167      parsed onto Policy
    scripts/lib/tier_policy.py:370         echoed by the `show` subcommand
    tests/unit/test_tier_policy_module.py  asserts the pattern compiles/matches

No workflow and no shell script reads it, and `validate_fork_pr` never consults
`policy.tier1_paths_regex` — a safe-tier-1 PR touching arbitrary paths validates
`ok`. Confirmed by editing the regex to exclude a path and watching
`validate_fork_pr` still pass it.

So the file's own comment tells a reader this value gates tier-1 eligibility
when it gates nothing. That is worse than an unused constant: a 2026-08-07 tick
inherited a note diagnosing a stuck findings PR as "the tier-1 regex cannot
match findings/items/*.json", wrote the widening fix and a test, and only caught
it because the test that should have gone red stayed green. The real blocker was
an ordinary merge conflict.

Decide one way or the other: either wire the regex into `validate_fork_pr` as
the comment claims, with tests, or delete it and drop the claim from the header.
Do not leave it looking load-bearing.
title: TIER1_PATHS_REGEX is declared as tier policy but enforces nothing
